name: Pork Cuts
summary: Lean loin cuts to cook quickly, fatty shoulder and belly to cook slowly, and why pork can be a little pink.

sections.heading: Pink pork is fine
blocks: Today's pork is much leaner and safer than it was a generation ago, and the USDA lowered its safe temperature for whole cuts (chops, tenderloin, loin roasts) to 145°F (63°C) with a 3-minute rest. At that point the middle is juicy and may still be blushing pink. Cooking chops to 160°F (71°C), as people used to, is why so many remember pork as dry.

blocks.text: Ground pork and sausages are different: cook them to 160°F (71°C). See the [doneness chart](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#doneness-chart).

sections.heading: Brining lean pork
blocks: Lean cuts (chops, loin) stay juicier after a brine. Dissolve 50 g of salt (3 Tbsp table salt, ¼ cup Morton kosher or ⅓ cup Diamond Crystal kosher) and a tablespoon of sugar in 4 cups (1 liter) of water, submerge the pork, and refrigerate for 30 minutes (chops) to 4 hours (a loin roast). Rinse, pat very dry, and season without extra salt.

blocks.text: Many supermarket cuts are already "enhanced" (injected with salt water); the label says so. Don't brine those, or they'll be too salty.
